{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1Hf3d25JHV64SevCPw8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs with OpenMP unconditionally. Its output is bitwise identical to the original, and it's about 17x faster than the original even on one thread. Scaling is close to linear through 16–32 threads.\n\n**Changes (only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt`):**\n- **`matrixMultiply`**: rows of C are split across threads with `#pragma omp parallel for`, so no two threads write the same element. The loop is now i-k-j with k-blocking (256), which makes the inner loop contiguous and vectorizable instead of striding down columns of B. Each `C[i][j]` still accumulates over k in ascending order.\n- **`initMatrix`**: parallelized with `collapse(2)`. Each element is independent, so this is deterministic.\n- **Validation, printing, and the timed region** are unchanged and still serial. The timed region is only `matrixMultiply`, as before.\n- **CMake**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)`, linked via `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` alongside `m`. There is no option to turn it off. The executable is still `matmul`.\n\n**One behavior change to know about: `-ffp-contract=off` is added to the compile flags.** With the default, GCC fused some multiply-adds in the original and left others unfused, depending on loop shape. The new loop shape produced different last bits, and no rewrite can reliably reproduce the original's mixed pattern. With the flag, each `a*b + c` is two rounded operations, as the source literally says. The consequence is that the original's `-r` hash (for example, N=17 gives `2a38b8b76fed35bb` without the flag and `4b77475f4d615384` with it) will differ from what the unmodified build printed. If you need the old hash, drop the flag, but then the output is compiler-dependent and the parallel result won't match the serial one exactly.\n\n**Verification** (builds and runs in `/tmp`; the repo has no new files):\n- Built the original and new versions with the same flags. Compared the `-r` output (hash, sum, min, max, samples) for N = 1, 2, 3, 7, 17, 100, 255, 256, 257, 300, 512, 777, 1000, 1024 at 1, 2, 4, 16, and 256 threads. All identical.\n- `-v` validation passes for the sizes I tried.\n- Build has no warnings with `-Wall -Wextra`.\n\n**Performance (GFLOPS, machine has 256 logical CPUs):**\n\n| N | original (serial) | new, 1 thread | new, 8 threads | new, 32 threads |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 0.38 | 6.7 | 44.7 | 89.5 |\n| 1024 | 0.26 | 6.4 | 45.7 | 153.4 |\n| 2048 | 0.17 | 4.3 | 26.7 | 73.7 |\n\nI didn't tune the block size or try wider register blocking, so there's likely more headroom at larger N. `common/results_output.hpp` is untouched; its Kahan sum runs outside the timed region and stays serial."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":841,"cache_read_input_tokens":33008,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":841},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ab18eaf5-5668-4a3b-afc1-917645529016","uuid":"e05be26b-4c84-4e43-bb1b-e9ed48087c53","timestamp":"2026-10-14T01:48:23.373Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1Hf3EDee7FZFc1cNgTR"}
